Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-20
Time: 10:00–10:42 UTC

Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Valerie Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Orion ML Eng), Trevor Huang (Orion Head of AI), Rita Patel (Orion PM)

Summary (auto):
Quick weekly POC sync focused on model selection and version pinning. Reviewed recent benchmark runs (latency/cost), discussed fallback/rollback strategy for live pilot, clarified VPC/network requirements and KMS expectations. Agreed on a 48-hour stability test pinned to rdx-3b-q4; Redwood to share bench spreadsheets and pricing/pilot amendment.

Topics: model selection, version pinning, rollbacks/fallbacks, KV-cache tuning, batching, VPC/KMS, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh we have about 40 minutes today so we can run through the bench results and next steps for the pinning tests. Maya, Trevor, you ok on time?
[00:12] Maya: yeah good to go. thanks Samir.
[00:15] Trevor: all good.
[00:18] Valerie: cool, i'll kick off with the numbers if that's okay. quick note, some of the auto-transcript in the bench sheet munged a couple of model names — rdx-3b-q4 shows up as r d x three b q four in the csv, sorry.
[00:31] Maya: yeah we saw that, but it's fine.
[00:33] Valerie: alright, so we re-ran the latency suite against three catalog candidates: rdx-3b-q4 (quantized), rdx-7b-fp16, and rdx-7b-q8. across our sample workload (average prompt length 120 tokens, 1-shot prompts) the median p95 latency was: rdx-3b-q4 ~ 120ms per token, rdx-7b-q8 ~ 180ms, rdx-7b-fp16 ~ 220ms. cost per 1k tokens showed rdx-3b-q4 was lowest at roughly $0.22, q8 about $0.35, fp16 about $0.48.
[01:12] Rita: so 3b looks attractive cost-wise. are we seeing any quality regressions?
[01:18] Valerie: good question. on our eval set the 3b has a small hit on reasoning anchors — maybe a drop of 4–6% on multi-step retrieval tasks. however for the customer-service style generation (the main Orion use case) the BLEU/semantic-sim scores are within noise. there are a couple of edge-case hallucinations that popped up more on the 3b.
[01:42] Maya: can you point to an example?
[01:44] Valerie: yeah, example in the sheet (row 432) where the 3b invented an internal sku mapping. 7b variants didn't. but we also tried a prefix-cache tweak and it reduced that failure rate by ~30%.
[02:01] Samir: ok, so sounds like tradeoff is cost/latency vs edge-case accuracy. what did you all think about pinning strategy for the pilot?
[02:09] Trevor: prefer pinning to rdx-3b-q4 but with a fallback policy to 7b-q8 on lower confidence or on high-latency paths. also want a quick rollback plan if we see regressions in production.
[02:22] Maya: agreed. we also want the ability to A/B test a small percentage against fp16 7b to verify user-visible quality.
[02:29] Rita: timeline-wise, we'd like to get the pilot in staging next week and production pilot the week after, assuming no showstoppers.
[02:36] Valerie: that seems reasonable. for the fallback rule we recommended — confidence threshold + latency threshold. if token generation stalls or confidence below 0.6 then route to 7b-q8. (we'll provide exact thresholds in the doc)
[02:52] Samir: and the routing can be done server-side in the Redwood control plane with automatic fallback?
[02:56] Valerie: yes, Redwood can do policy-based routing. we can set canary percentages too. but note that switching increases cost when fallback triggers, so do expect spikes.
[03:08] Trevor: on failover — how fast is a rollback if something goes wrong? like do we need infra changes?
[03:14] Valerie: if it's model rollout within Redwood hosted or dedicated, rollback is usually minutes — we flip the route config and the control plane will route to a pinned stable variant. for private VPC installs, we'd need to coordinate with your infra team, but still we can script a quick rollback; maybe 20–40 minutes depending on approvals.
[03:31] Maya: regarding VPC, we had a couple questions about KMS and audit logs. our security team needs to confirm key rotation support and HSM options.
[03:40] Samir: yeah we'll include SOC2 and KMS integration notes. Valerie, do we have the KMS docs link?
[03:45] Valerie: i'll attach it after the call. quick note — on private deployments we support customer-managed KMS via the usual providers; HSM options require enterprise package.
[03:56] Rita: ok good. and audit logging — would that be per-request logs, or aggregated? we need request-level traces for compliance.
[04:04] Valerie: we can enable request-level audit logs; retention is configurable per plan. for the pilot we can enable 30 days. longer retention is an add-on.
[04:13] Maya: back to bench — did you run a continuous run to see KV-cache warmup effects? our production mix has a lot of repeated prefixes so caching should help.
[04:22] Valerie: yes we did a 6-hour continuous run. rdx-3b-q4 saw ~40% token-level cost reduction after warm cache, 7b variants ~25%. so the smaller model benefits more from caching due to prefix repetition patterns.
[04:36] Trevor: that's useful. does Redwood do automated prefix caching or does it need per-model config?
[04:42] Valerie: automated by default, but you can tune TTLs and cache keys. we'll share recommended config.
[04:48] Samir: any throughput concerns for peak traffic? we had a spike test last Friday.
[04:52] Valerie: we saw sustained throughput of ~800 rps on dedicated pool for the 3b pinned config with batching at 64; p95 latency stayed under target. for hosted shared, it depends on burst capacity — you can request reserved capacity if you want predictable SLOs.
[05:07] Rita: cost question — can you show the delta between reserved and on-demand for the pilot?
[05:11] Samir: yes i'll include pricing examples. we'll show per-token and reserved commit discounts.
[05:17] Maya: another note — in our internal eval we saw a small but consistent tokenization mismatch for some product SKUs with the quantized model; might be because of token boundary changes. is that something you can investigate?
[05:29] Valerie: yeah we'll look. sometimes quantization changes can affect subword handling but usually it's consistent; we'll run the SKU-focused pass.
[05:36] Trevor: on the fallback routing, does it preserve user context if it switches to 7b? we need to avoid losing KV-cache.
[05:44] Valerie: good point. we support KV cache migration between compatible variants if they share tokenizer and architecture family; it'll add a small latency cost during switch. we'll document specifics and caveats.
[05:57] Samir: ok. i'm thinking about the rollback and monitoring plan — what metrics should we watch during the 48-hour pinned run?
[06:06] Valerie: latency p50/p95, error rates, hallucination/regression rate from prompt set, fallback trigger rate, cost per 1k tokens, and tokenization mismatch counts. also set alerts at 20% degradation for quality signals.
[06:23] Rita: can Redwood stream evaluation logs to our S3? we'd like to ingest them into our observability.
[06:29] Valerie: yes, we can push logs to your S3 or set up an event hook into your pipeline.
[06:33] Maya: on canaries, we want to test 5% traffic on rdx-3b-q4 with 95% on 7b-q8 for two days — to compare user metrics. is that doable?
[06:43] Valerie: yes, we can configure that. keep in mind cost-weighting in the dashboards will autofill.
[06:48] Trevor: any red flags on security posture? we reviewed SOC2 doc earlier and it looked fine.
[06:53] Samir: we'll also include ISO docs and the SOC2 report in the next email.
[06:58] Maya: cool. one more question — when you say rdx-3b-q4, is there a build tag we can pin to? we want immutable artifacts not floating tags.
[07:06] Valerie: great callout. yes we provision immutable model versions with hash tags. for the pilot we'll provide the exact model version id (e.g., rdx-3b-q4@2027-10-18-commit-ab12). pinning will reference that id.
[07:18] Rita: good. and for rollbacks we'll reference previous model id. perfect.
[07:22] Samir: alright, let's align on the 48-hour stability test pinned to rdx-3b-q4@2027-10-18-commit-ab12. Maya, you run the suite and share failures; Valerie sends config and thresholds. Samir sends pricing and pilot amendment.
[07:35] Maya: yep.
[07:36] Valerie: i'll attach the bench sheet and the prefix/kv tuning notes to the email after call. also will include a short runbook for rollback and fallback policies.
[07:47] Trevor: on the runbook — include contacts and escalation path, because our ops team wants a clear SLA.
[07:53] Valerie: will do.
[07:55] Samir: any final Qs?
[07:57] Rita: none from me.
[07:58] Maya: no.
[07:59] Trevor: okay all good.
[08:01] Samir: cool, we'll follow up. thanks everyone.
